root_cause.text: `xe_exec_queue_create_ioctl()` had incorrect error-unwind ordering in the DRM/xe exec-queue setup path, so failures after partially registering a queue could free `xe_exec_queue` objects without removing them from the VM’s compute-exec list or the hardware engine group list, leaving dangling links and causing use-after-free/dangling-pointer bugs.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the `xe_hw_engine_group_add_exec_queue()` failure path from `goto put_exec_queue` to `goto kill_exec_queue` because skipping `xe_exec_queue_kill()` leaves the queue on the VM compute exec queue list, and it adds a new `del_hw_engine_group` cleanup label before `kill_exec_queue` so that on `xa_alloc()` failure the code calls `xe_hw_engine_group_del_exec_queue()` before freeing the queue; the commit message explicitly states the old paths left the queue linked into those lists and led to dangling pointer/UAF conditions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the error cleanup path for exec queue creation when hw engine group registration fails.
intent_record.what: In xe_exec_queue_create_ioctl(), the error path after xe_hw_engine_group_add_exec_queue() fails was changed from jumping to put_exec_queue to jumping to kill_exec_queue.
intent_record.how: If adding the exec queue to the hardware engine group fails, the function now takes a different cleanup path that is presumably more complete or appropriate for a partially initialized queue, altering the teardown behavior during error handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix exec queue creation failure cleanup by removing the queue from its hardware engine group before killing it.
intent_record.what: The error path after `xa_alloc(&xef->exec_queue.xa, &id, q, xa_limit_32b, GFP_KERNEL)` was changed from jumping directly to `kill_exec_queue` to jumping to a new `del_hw_engine_group` label. A new cleanup block was added that conditionally calls `xe_hw_engine_group_del_exec_queue(q->hwe->hw_engine_group, q)` when `q->vm`, `q->hwe`, and `q->hwe->hw_engine_group` are present, before falling through to the existing `kill_exec_queue` cleanup.
intent_record.how: If exec queue ID allocation fails, the code now also removes the queue from its hardware engine group before killing the queue. This prevents the queue from remaining registered in the hardware engine group during teardown, ensuring cleanup is performed in the correct order and avoiding stale state or resource leakage on the failure path.

grouping_result.intent: Fix exec queue creation failure cleanup by removing the queue from its hardware engine group before killing it.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body already contains the new hw-engine-group registration and cleanup logic, which addresses the described dangling-link/UAF issue. In `xe_exec_queue_create_ioctl()` the queue is added to the group only after earlier setup succeeds: `if (q->vm && q->hwe->hw_engine_group) { err = xe_hw_engine_group_add_exec_queue(q->hwe->hw_engine_group, q); if (err) goto put_exec_queue; }`. This is the fix for tracking the queue in the group list. The destroy path also removes it before freeing: `if (q->vm && q->hwe->hw_engine_group) xe_hw_engine_group_del_exec_queue(q->hwe->hw_engine_group, q);`. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause—freeing a partially registered exec queue without removing it from the hw-engine-group list—is not present here, because the delete path is now explicit and happens before `xe_exec_queue_kill(q)`. Therefore the function body reflects the fixed behavior, not the bug.
